Common recruitment & radicalization patterns (high-level)
1. Exploiting grievances and identity struggles
Targeting individuals who feel marginalized, isolated, or wronged
Framing personal frustrations as part of a larger “injustice” narrative
2. Gradual exposure to ideology
Introducing ideas slowly rather than all at once
Starting with seemingly benign content before moving toward more extreme beliefs
3. Use of online spaces
Leveraging social media, forums, gaming platforms, or encrypted apps
Creating echo chambers where extreme views feel normalized
4. Personal connection and grooming
Building trust through friendship, mentorship, or romantic interest
Providing emotional support, then steering beliefs over time
5. Propaganda and storytelling
Using emotionally charged narratives, videos, or symbols
Portraying violence as justified, heroic, or necessary
6. “Us vs. them” framing
Simplifying the world into clear enemies and allies
Dehumanizing out-groups to reduce moral barriers
7. Isolation from alternative viewpoints
Encouraging recruits to distrust family, media, or institutions
Reinforcing dependence on the group for “truth”
8. Promises of purpose or belonging
Offering identity, status, or meaning (e.g., “you’ll be part of something bigger”)
Appealing especially to those lacking direction or community
Why this matters
Understanding these patterns helps:
Recognize early warning signs
Support at-risk individuals
Build resilience against manipulation
